Another open problem concerns the optimization landscape of practical MGDL implementations, in which network parameters are learned from data rather than constructed analytically, and how such training dynamics affect stability and generalization.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem selects weights analytically from the entire target function; it does not show that the grade-wise minimizations select these weights or preserve their information-carrying structure. For the stated finite-sample procedure, a continuous nonzero target can vanish at every training point. Choosing T_1 and all outputs identically zero then attains zero empirical MSE at every grade, while the uniform approximation error remains positive. Thus even exact grade-wise minimization does not supply the advertised training guarantee.

failure_location.quote: To the best of our knowledge, this work provides the first rigorous theoretical guarantee that grade-wise training yields provable vanishing approximation error in deep networks.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the guarantee to analytically constructed approximation sequences and distinguish it explicitly from convergence of grade-wise minimization or Adam training. Retaining the training claim requires new optimization and information-preservation hypotheses and results.
issues.overall_effect: Independently of the approximation-proof defects, convergence of the specified optimization or data-training procedure is not established.
issues.title: An approximation construction is presented as a training-convergence guarantee
issues.why_classification: The supported correction changes an optimization-convergence guarantee into an existence guarantee for specially chosen weights, a major change in guarantee type.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:

issues.failure_explanation: No attainment hypothesis is imposed on the dictionary. In Euclidean R², take R_0=(1,0) and atoms e_n=(1,1/n), n≥1. The best error using e_n is 1/sqrt(n²+1), so the infimum over atoms is zero but no atom attains it. Normalizing the atoms does not change this example. The displayed argmin can therefore be empty.

issues.overall_effect: The stated exact greedy procedure is not well defined for all dictionaries permitted by its formulation.
issues.title: Exact greedy dictionary selection need not attain its minimum
issues.why_classification: A standard local well-posedness qualification suffices for this illustrative procedure; no new approximation theorem or convergence analysis is required.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
For notational convenience, we denote by $\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{MGDL}}(k)$ the
subset of $\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{MGDL}}$ consisting of compositions of the form
$T_k \circ \cdots \circ T_1$.

issues.failure_explanation: Optimality of one atom does not imply that another atom from the same dictionary can only marginally improve the residual. On [0,1], consider one-unit ReLU blocks with affine outputs, the uniform norm, and f(x)=|2x−1|. Every such one-unit output is monotone, so its best uniform error is at least 1/2. The atom h_1(x)=ReLU(2x−1)+1/2 attains that bound, but its residual is exactly h_2(x)=ReLU(1−2x)−1/2, another atom in the same class. A second atom eliminates the entire residual without increasing atom depth.

failure_location.quote:
Finally, it is important to note that after $k-1$ iterations, the composition

Simply selecting another atom from this fixed space would therefore yield only

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Limit the assertion to reoptimization within the fixed linear span of already frozen features after an exact fit. Do not extend it to selecting different atoms from the same compositional dictionary.

issues.failure_explanation: For d≥2, take a nonzero continuous bump supported strictly inside the cube, such as the product of max(1−4|x_j−1/2|,0). At k=1, pointwise domination forces the one-hidden-layer correction h_1 to vanish on an open collar of the cube boundary. A finite affine combination of ReLU ridge functions has constant gradient jumps along whole hyperplanes. Every hyperplane meeting the interior support also meets that collar, where its jump must vanish; after grouping coincident hyperplanes, all such jumps cancel. Hence h_1 is affine on the cube and, being zero on the collar, is identically zero. Strict first-step Lp decrease is therefore impossible. This obstruction remains even if the cutoff construction is corrected.
